title: Integer Overflow and Truncation in Allocation
platform_conditions: C99/C11 on any hosted toolchain; signed overflow is undefined behavior (optimizers may remove the guard), unsigned overflow wraps silently
security_mechanism: Allocation sizes are computed in machine integers before malloc sees them: `count * elem_size` on a 32-bit or 64-bit width wraps modulo 2^N, so two large attacker-supplied values multiply to a small total and the allocation succeeds with a fraction of the needed storage. Later writes indexed by the original count then run off the end of the small block. Mixing signed int with size_t truncates or sign-extends: a negative int converted to size_t becomes a huge unsigned value, and a value above INT_MAX reinterpreted after a check written for int passes a check the allocator never applies. Because signed overflow is undefined behavior, a check written after the multiplication can also be optimized away.

source_sink_clues.source: Counts, element sizes, or lengths taken from protocol fields, file headers, or array/loop parameters that the client controls (e.g. a number-of-items field followed by that many elements).
source_sink_clues.sink: malloc/calloc/realloc/alalloca called with a computed size; loop bounds and memcpy sizes derived from the same product

tracking_guards: Check that the multiplication uses a checked primitive (__builtin_mul_overflow, __builtin_add_overflow, or CERT-recommended pre-division check like `if (elem_size && count > SIZE_MAX / elem_size)`), that the result is held in size_t end to end, and that the count is bounded by an explicit protocol maximum before arithmetic.
not_candidate_when: The count is validated against a fixed protocol maximum well below the overflow threshold before any arithmetic, the element size is a compile-time constant and the count is already bounded, or the allocation feeds an internal batch job whose inputs no external party controls.
synthetic_vulnerable_example: size_t total = count * elem_size; void *p = malloc(total);
public_references: SEI CERT C Coding Standard: INT30-C (unsigned overflow), MEM35-C (allocation size check)
